title: Efficient Bitruss Decomposition without Butterfly Enumeration

problem.claim: Compute, for each edge in a given bipartite graph, the largest k for which the edge remains contained in a k-bitruss.

gap.claim: Existing state-of-the-art solutions must touch every butterfly at least once, incurring O(⧖G) cost, with the number of butterflies potentially reaching O(m2).

contributions.claim: BiT-DT is an algorithm for bitruss decomposition with running time bounded by O(m^1.5 log m).
The algorithm identifies the next edges to peel without maintaining precise butterfly support for every edge.
A batch-peeling heuristic is proposed to improve the practical performance of BiT-DT.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe BiT-DT as the first algorithm of its kind for this purpose.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on ten real-world datasets report that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by up to an order of magnitude in running time.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cohesive-subgraph mining in bipartite graphs supports applications including recommendation and fraud detection.
The paper studies bitruss decomposition and the largest k-bitruss value associated with each edge.
Prior peeling-based methods enumerate or touch all butterflies, and butterfly counts can be quadratic in the number of edges.
BiT-DT improves the stated asymptotic bound by selecting peelable edges without exact per-edge butterfly support and adds batch peeling.
Experiments on ten real-world datasets report up to an order-of-magnitude running-time improvement over state-of-the-art baselines.
